facts.fact_text: Some of the applications raise an issue concerning the right to freedom of peaceful assembly in connection with the applicants' protests against the landfill site near the town of Klin, Moscow Region.
In March 2018 the applicants started organising protests against the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
All the applicants except Ms Kotova (application no. 106/19) were charged with various administrative offences in connection with their protests against the landfill site.

In May 2018 Mr Kotov submitted one notice of an environmental protest car rally to the Klin municipal administration.
Neither of Mr Kotov's applications to the Klin municipal administration for a public event or environmental protest car rally was approved.

The right to a safe environment in Russia is contained in Article 42 of the Russian Constitution.

The right to bring civil or administrative proceedings by private persons or State bodies in respect of environmental damage in Russia is contained in Articles 1064 and 1065 of the Civil Code, Article 23.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences, Articles 39 and 218 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, and Article 42 of the Land Code.

The obligation of physical or legal persons to comply with relevant environmental regulations in Russia is contained in Articles 1064 and 1065 of the Civil Code, Article 23.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences, Articles 39 and 218 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, and Article 42 of the Land Code.
Articles 56 and 57 of the Russian Civil Procedure Code govern issues of presenting and collecting evidence in civil proceedings.

Ruling of the Russian Supreme Court no. 1 of 26 January 2010 contains detailed provisions concerning compensation of harm to life or health of physical persons and compensation for environmental damage.

Ruling of the Russian Supreme Court no. 49 of 30 November 2017 contains detailed provisions concerning compensation of harm to life or health of physical persons and compensation for environmental damage.
Federal Law no. 174-FZ of 23 November 1995 regulates environmental impact assessments for various industrial projects made by State bodies or public interest organisations in Russia.
Federal Law no. 89-FZ of 24 June 1998 regulates matters relating to industrial and household waste, including registration of landfills in the State landfill register, in Russia.
Federal Law no. 52-FZ of 12 March 1999 regulates the sanitary and epidemiological well-being of the population in Russia.
Federal Law no. 96-FZ of 4 May 1999 regulates air pollution, including the requirement of industrial self-monitoring, in Russia.

Federal Law no. 7-FZ of 10 January 2002 regulates the protection of the environment in Russia, covering types of polluting entities, the requirement of industrial self-monitoring, the right to information, the right to protest, the right to compensation, and the right to bring complaints.
Federal Law no. 99-FZ of 4 May 2011 regulates the licensing of activities of waste-processing operators in Russia.

Decree no. 322 of 30 June 2004 and State Decree no. 476 of 5 June 2013 (as in force before 30 June 2021) regulate the Federal Consumer Protection Authority's supervisory and preventative functions in the environmental sphere, including dealing with complaints about unfavourable environmental conditions, in Russia.
Sanitary Regulations 2.2.1/2.1.1.1200-03 of 25 September 2007 regulate environmental protection zones around polluting enterprises in Russia.
The applicants alleged that the large numbers of scavenging birds at the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry had threatened air safety in the area.
A military airbase known as Klin-5 was situated within 3 km of the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

Representatives of the Ministry of Defence had requested the regional government of Moscow Region to have Aleksinskiy Quarry closed because its use had endangered the safety of military planes from Klin-5 airbase during their flights, owing to the circulation of birds above the quarry.

The authorities stated in reply to the Ministry of Defence's request that there were no grounds to close Aleksinskiy Quarry since the modern waste processing plant would be installed by 2021 and the quarry would no longer pose a danger to aircraft.
In March 2018 the applicants started organising protests against the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
All the applicants except Ms Kotova (application no. 106/19) were charged with various administrative offences in connection with their protests against the landfill site.
In November 2017 Mr Kotov submitted three notices of a public event (meeting) to the Klin municipal administration.
In May 2018 Mr Kotov submitted one notice of an environmental protest car rally to the Klin municipal administration.
Neither of Mr Kotov's applications to the Klin municipal administration for a public event or environmental protest car rally was approved.
Mr Kotov brought a complaint against the Klin municipal authorities before the courts in connection with the non-approval of his applications for public events.
The details of the proceedings brought by Mr Kotov against the Klin municipal authorities are outlined in Appendix I (application no. 56764/18) of the judgment.

In a letter of 10 April 2013 addressed to the Russian President, the regional governor of Moscow Region highlighted the deteriorating environmental situation in Moscow Region and the need to implement modern waste processing technologies.

In a letter of 10 April 2013 addressed to the Russian President, the regional governor of Moscow Region requested the President to order the closure of twenty-four landfills in Moscow Region owing to their excessive storage capacity and obsolete technical characteristics.

Between 18 March 2016 and 29 April 2019 the regional and municipal authorities, including representatives of the Committee on the Environment of Moscow Region legislative authority, held eighteen public meetings in the form of hearings, assize legislative sessions and discussions in respect of operations at Aleksinskiy Quarry and its modernisation.

On 29 April 2019 a public hearing was held on the project for the construction of a waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry in order to obtain the views of residents, including those of the applicants, who provided their observations and objections on the issue.
Following the public hearing of 29 April 2019, the project documentation for the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry was sent for a State environmental impact assessment.

On 28 January 2016 the Regional Minister of Natural Resources and the Environment of Moscow Region, during a meeting with residents of Klin and official representatives of Kombinat LLC, stated that the main complaint by residents was the smell emanating from Aleksinskiy Quarry.

On 28 January 2016 the Regional Minister of Natural Resources and the Environment of Moscow Region stated that waste disposal operations at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been carried out in violation of the applicable regulations.

On 28 January 2016 the Regional Minister of Natural Resources and the Environment of Moscow Region stated that the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry appeared to be the only solution to the environmental problems caused by the quarry.
